# Knee-Friendly Weekly Health Tracker

A simple tracker can help you build fitness while watching for patterns in sleep, pain, and activity. This plan uses low-impact training, recovery days, and a 7-day log format you can repeat each week.

# Weekly Tracker Layout and Sample Log

## 7-Day Sample Log
| Day | Steps | Sleep Hours | Pain Score (0-10) | Exercise Type |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Mon | 7,200 | 7.5 | 3 | Easy walk + mobility |
| Tue | 8,100 | 7.0 | 4 | Cycling, low resistance |
| Wed | 6,400 | 8.0 | 2 | Strength: upper body + core |
| Thu | 9,000 | 6.8 | 5 | Short run/walk intervals |
| Fri | 7,800 | 7.4 | 3 | Brisk walk + stretching |
| Sat | 10,200 | 8.2 | 2 | Longer bike ride |
| Sun | 5,900 | 8.5 | 1 | Rest + gentle mobility |

## Visualization Plan
- **Sleep bar chart**
  - X-axis: Day
  - Y-axis: Sleep hours
  - Goal line: 7.5–8.0 hours
  - Use bars to spot low-sleep days before higher pain days

- **Pain-score line chart**
  - X-axis: Day
  - Y-axis: Pain score 0–10
  - Add a reference band for 0–3 as “manageable”
  - Watch for spikes after impact workouts or poor sleep

- **Activity pie chart**
  - Categories: Walking, Cycling, Strength, Run/Walk, Mobility, Rest
  - Use weekly totals or time spent
  - Aim for most activity in low-impact categories, with running kept modest

## Weekly Pattern Summary
- Pain is lowest on **rest, mobility, and cycling** days.
- Pain rises after the **run/walk interval** day, especially when sleep is shorter.
- Better sleep appears to match **lower pain scores** and better recovery.
- The week is already balanced enough to build fitness, but the highest-impact session should be the smallest part of the plan.

## Non-Medical Next Steps
- Keep running **short and easy** for now; use run/walk intervals instead of continuous runs.
- Shift most cardio to **cycling, brisk walking, or elliptical** to reduce knee load.
- Add **2 strength sessions** weekly focused on glutes, hips, calves, and core.
- Track pain **before and 24 hours after exercise** to see which workouts are most irritating.
- Use a simple rule: if pain is trending upward for several days, reduce impact and volume for the next week.
- Prioritize **sleep consistency**, since recovery seems to track with lower pain.

## Quick Actions

- CDC physical activity basics: https://www.cdc.gov/physicalactivity/basics/index.htm
- NHS knee pain overview: https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/knee-pain/
- Mayo Clinic exercise and joint health: https://www.mayoclinic.org/healthy-lifestyle/fitness/in-depth/exercise/art-20045506
